pairs: Numquid nosti tempus partus ibicum in petris,
Do you know at what time the wild goats have given birth among the rocks,
or do you observe the deer when they go into labor?
Have you numbered the months since their conception,
and do you know at what time they gave birth?
They bend themselves for their offspring,
and do not return to them.
Who has set the wild ass free,
and who has released his bonds?
I have given a house in solitude to him,
et tabernacula ejus in terra salsuginis.
and his tabernacle is in the salted land.
he does not pay attention to the bellow of the tax collector.
He looks around the mountains of his pasture,
and he searches everywhere for green plants.
Will the rhinoceros be willing to serve you,
and will he remain in your stall?
Numquid alligabis rhinocerota ad arandum loro tuo,
Can you detain the rhinoceros with your harness to plough for you,
aut confringet glebas vallium post te?
and will he loosen the soil of the furrows behind you?
Numquid fiduciam habebis in magna fortitudine ejus,
Will you put your faith in his great strength,
and delegate your labors to him?
Numquid credes illi quod sementem reddat tibi,
Will you trust him to return to you the seed,
and to gather it on your drying floor?
Penna struthionis similis est pennis herodii
The wing of the ostrich is like the wings of the heron,
Quando derelinquit ova sua in terra,
When she leaves eggs behind in the earth,
tu forsitan in pulvere calefacies ea?
will you perhaps warm them in the dust?
She forgets that feet may trample them,
or that the beasts of the field may shatter them.
She is hardened against her young,
as if they were not hers;
For God has deprived her of wisdom;
neither has he given her understanding.
she raises her wings on high;
she ridicules the horse and his rider.
Will you supply strength to the horse,
or envelope his throat with neighing?
Will you alarm him as the locusts do?
His panic is revealed by the display of his nostrils.
He digs at the earth with his hoof;
he advances to meet armed men.
he does not turn away from the sword.
the spear and the shield shake.
neither does he pause when the blast of the trumpet sounds.
He smells the battle from a distance,
and the battle cry of the soldiers.
Numquid per sapientiam tuam plumescit accipiter,
Does the hawk grow feathers by means of your wisdom,
spreading her wings towards the south?
Numquid ad præceptum tuum elevabitur aquila,
Will the eagle lift herself up at your command
et in arduis ponet nidum suum?
and make her nest in steep places?
and she lingers among broken boulders
From there, she looks for food,
et de longe oculi ejus prospiciunt.
and her eyes catch sight of it from far away.
and wherever the carcass will be,
Numquid qui contendit cum Deo, tam facile conquiescit?
Will he who contends with God be so easily silenced? Certainly,
utique qui arguit Deum, debet respondere ei.
he who argues with God must also respond to him.
since I have been speaking thoughtlessly?
manum meam ponam super os meum.
I will place my hand over my mouth.
which I wish I had not said;
to which I will add no more.
